questions.question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

(A) the concert was too expensive

(B) to watch his favourite

(C) hard-earned money

(D) to waste his parents'

(E) artist's live performance

(F) so he sacrificed the chance
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **ADCFBE**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct sequence of the sentence is: 
 
 
• **A **- "The concert was too expensive"
 
• **D **- "to waste his parents'"
 
• **C **- "hard-earned money"
 
• **F **- "so he sacrificed the chance"
 
• **B **- "to watch his favourite"
 
• **E **- "artist's live performance"
 
 
 
• When sequenced correctly, the sentence reads:
 
 
• "The concert was too expensive to waste his parents' hard-earned money on, so he sacrificed the chance to watch his favourite artist's live performance."
 
 
 
• This order logically and grammatically connects each part, providing a clear cause-and-effect relationship, and describing a situation where the cost of the concert influenced the person's decision to forgo attending the performance.

questions.question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

A: leaped into the water

B: ship touched the shore

C: as soon as the

D: a soldier of the tenth legion
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option (4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence begins with "a soldier of the tenth legion," which is correctly indicated by **part (D)** as it introduces the main subject of the sentence.** **
 
• Following the action, "leaped into the water" **(A)**
 
• **The next part,** "as soon as the" **(C)** sets up a condition that needs to be **completed.**
 
• **Ending with, ** "ship touched the shore" **(B),** completes the condition by describing when the action took place.

Therefore, the correct sentence is: **"A**** soldier of the tenth legion, leaped into the water as soon as the ship touched the shore."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (BDAC):** This option starts with "ship touched the shore," which places the event before the subject, making the sentence confusing and incomplete.
 
• **Option 2 (ACBD):** This option starts with "leaped into the water," which does not provide a context for who is performing the action and when it is happening, making the sentence unclear.
 
• **Option 3 (CBDA):** This option starts with "as soon as the," which should be part of the condition, but without a subject at the beginning, it creates an incomplete sentence structure.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice.

The wild elephant will be captured and left in the forest.

options.text: They will capture the wild elephant and leave it in the forest.
We had captured and left the wild elephant in the forest.
The wild elephant would be captured by us and left in the forest.
We would have captured and left the wild elephant in the forest.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence in the passive voice is converted to the active voice by making the subject (they) perform the action.
 
• The correct active voice sentence is: **"They will capture the wild elephant and leave it in the forest."**
 
• **Options 2, 3**, and 4 do not correctly convert the sentence to active voice.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"They will capture the wild elephant and leave it in the forest."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "We had captured and left the wild elephant in the forest" uses past perfect tense, which is incorrect for this context.
 
• **Option 3:** "The wild elephant would be captured by us and left in the forest" still retains the passive voice structure.
 
• **Option 4:** "We would have captured and left the wild elephant in the forest" uses conditional perfect tense, which is not suitable here.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Rakesh appointed three managers.

options.text: Three managers were appointed by Rakesh.
Three managers will be appointed by Rakesh.
Three managers were being appointed by Rakesh.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Three managers were appointed by Rakesh.**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in active voice: "**Rakesh appointed three managers**."
 
• In passive voice, the object of the action ("**three managers**") becomes the subject.
 
• The verb "**appointed**" is changed to "**were appointed**" to match the plural subject.
 
• "**by Rakesh**" is added to indicate who performed the action.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"Three managers were appointed by Rakesh."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "Three managers will be appointed by Rakesh"** is incorrect because it uses future tense.
 
• **Option 3: "Three managers were being appointed by Rakesh"** is incorrect because it uses past continuous tense.
 
• **Option 4: "Three managers appointed Rakesh"** is incorrect because it reverses the subject and object.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

She said, “I am going to Delhi to attend my friend’s marriage.”

options.text: She said that she was going to Delhi to attend my friend’s marriage.
She said that she was going to Delhi to attend our friend’s marriage.
She said that I was going to Delhi to attend my friend’s marriage.
She said that she was going to Delhi to attend her friend’s marriage.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**She said that she was going to Delhi to attend her friend's marriage**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To convert direct speech into indirect speech, we need to change the present tense verbs to their past tense forms.
 
• In this case, "I am" changes to "she was" and "my friend's" changes to "her friend's."
 
• **Options 1, 2**, and 3 are incorrect as they do not properly convert the pronouns and verbs to their correct forms.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"She said that she was going to Delhi to attend her friend's marriage."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "she was going to Delhi to attend my friend's marriage" is incorrect because "my" should change to "her" in indirect speech.
 
• **Option 2:** "she was going to Delhi to attend our friend's marriage" is incorrect because "our" should change to "her" in indirect speech.
 
• **Option 3:** "I was going to Delhi to attend my friend's marriage" is incorrect because "I" should change to "she" and "my" should change to "her" in indirect speech.
